item.title: 🟠 Scans for Sshole Vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158), (Sun, Nov 8th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Early technical signal — worth a quick scan for issues that may become more important.

Our honeypots use "Cowrie" to collect SSH data. With the emergence of the "sshole" vulnerability last week, we are now seeing an increase in attempts to exploit the vulnerability. Our data is a bit limited in this respect. Our honeypots collect only the first 255 characters of SSH passwords. Longer passwords are highly unusual and not used for the usual password brute-forcing we observe.



Source: SANS Internet Storm Center  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 8h

item.title: 🟠 The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts, (Wed, Nov 4th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Early technical signal — worth a quick scan for issues that may become more important.

One of the early web application vulnerabilities I remember was CVE-2000-0411 [CVE]. This was a simple vulnerability in a CGI-bin script used to send e-mail. The vulnerability was pretty straightforward: Adding additional parameters to the URL leaked environment variables. Other vulnerabilities allowed setting the "To" address and were heavily abused by spammers. And if parameters were passed directly to the sendmail binary, similar vulnerabilities could allow arbitrary code execution.



Source: SANS Internet Storm Center  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 4d

item.title: 🟠 Bias in Qwen3-Coder Model
item.description:
Why this matters: Early technical signal — worth a quick scan for issues that may become more important.

Interesting research:

TL;DR: Chinese AI models now sit inside Western products, and some carry geopolitical triggers: tell the model who the code is for, and the security of what it writes changes. For the first time, we showed that this vulnerability lives in the model’s weights, and that removing the model’s CCP alignment removes it.

  • One word tilts the code against Americans. Ask for the app “for a US defense contractor” instead of “for a Chinese defense contractor”, and Qwen3-Coder is 19% more likely to hand back an app that can be hacked. ...


Source: Schneier on Security  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 13d
